output_json.patch_notes: Added a private isChildOfBase(File) helper in FileResourceManager that compares file.getCanonicalPath() against new File(base).getCanonicalPath() (exact match or proper descendant via File.separator prefix), called right after `new File(base, path)` / `file.exists()` and before the existing case-sensitivity check and FileResource construction. Any resolution that escapes `base` now returns null instead of a Resource. Added FileResourceManagerTestCase (plain JUnit, no server harness needed) verifying: (1) a normal in-base resource is still served, (2) forward-slash traversal variants ("/../secret.txt", "/a/../../secret.txt", "../secret.txt") are blocked, (3) backslash-delimited traversal variants are blocked (meaningfully exercised on Windows; on Linux they degrade to a nonexistent single-segment filename, which is already null, so the test still documents/enforces the invariant cross-platform). Verified against the provided POV harness: before the fix it printed VULNERABLE (exit 0); after the fix it prints "SAFE: getResource(\"/../secret.txt\") returned null (traversal blocked)" (exit 1). Full `mvn -B -DskipTests package` build succeeds across all modules (core, servlet, examples, websockets-jsr).
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk: the added check only rejects resolutions whose canonical path falls outside the configured base directory — legitimate in-base requests (including symlinks that resolve to a location still under base) are unaffected, confirmed by existing FileHandlerTestCase/FileHandlerIndexTestCase passing unchanged. One behavior change to be aware of: if `base` itself is configured as (or contains) a symlink whose target is intentionally outside the nominal base path, and callers rely on serving through that symlink to an external directory, this fix would now block those requests, since containment is computed against base's own canonical path. This matches the security intent of the alert (no silent escape from the configured resource root) and is the standard mitigation pattern for this CWE class. No dependency or API surface changes; only internal behavior of FileResourceManager.getResource tightened.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal at the shared root cause: FileResourceManager.getResource(String) resolved `new File(base, path)` and returned a FileResource with no check that the resolved file actually stayed within `base` — only a last-path-segment case check existed. Added a canonical-path containment check (isChildOfBase) immediately after file resolution: the resolved file's canonical path must equal the canonical base directory or be a descendant of it (via File.separator-based prefix match), otherwise getResource returns null before any Resource is constructed. Since all four alert traces (direct ResourceHandler calls, ServletContextImpl.getRealPath, and both DefaultServlet.getPath variants) converge on this exact sink, the fix blocks every path in the alert without needing to patch each caller individually. Because the check relies on java.io.File's own platform-correct canonicalization/separator handling, it also closes the Windows-specific backslash bypass path (CanonicalPathUtils only handling '/') without needing changes to CanonicalPathUtils itself — the sink now refuses escapes regardless of what separator smuggled the ".." through.
